cells.tense: What you built is standing here now, and you are meeting it on time.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that finished arriving this week and say, out loud or in your own notes, which way you're steering it from here.
cells.core: Something you set in motion has finished arriving. Not the idea of it — the actual thing, with weight and edges, in the room with you. You can let it be what it is without shrinking it or needing it to be more. That's what carrying it looks like when it's going well: you keep choosing the heading while the arrival is still warm.\n\nSame move today. Name one thing that's fully here now and say which way it's pointed from here. It doesn't have to be a big turn. One sentence, one direction, said while the thing is still fresh in the room. Keep saying it tomorrow and the direction holds; stop, and the arrival starts deciding for you.
cells.sheetLine: The arrival is real and you're still steering it.
cells.place: the opening where what's arriving comes in

cells.tense: You're bracing for a version that hasn't arrived, and the bracing is taking up the room it needs.
cells.ask: When tomorrow's draft tries to walk in today, close the door on it once. See what's actually in the room.
cells.core: You're holding a shape for something that isn't here yet. The next version, the finished one, the one that will finally be right — you've made room for it, and the room it took is today's. The weight you're carrying is rehearsal for a load nobody handed you.\n\nWhat meets an arrival has tilted forward past it, and the tilt is what's costing you. This isn't about relaxing. Pick one moment today and let the next version stay out of it — one conversation, one hour. Meet what's actually there before you decide what it is. The present gets clearer when you stop standing in for a future that hasn't happened yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying tomorrow's load in today's room.
cells.place: the opening where what's arriving comes in

cells.tense: Something already arrived and you're still standing at the door you came through.
cells.ask: Open one thing that finished — the folder, the message, the box — and sit with it for fifteen minutes where it already is.
cells.core: Something got delivered and you didn't open it. The work landed, or the change did, and part of you is still back at the starting line deciding whether any of it counts. Sitting in the room it made, feeling its edges, letting it be true for a minute before you decide anything about it — that's the whole of it, done well. The door is behind you and you're still facing it.\n\nNothing needs an audience here. There's no arriving to rehearse, only noticing what's already in. Pick one piece that finished, the one you keep walking past, and stay with it until you feel something about it. Not a verdict. Just contact. The way back is through the door you're already past.
cells.sheetLine: It arrived while you were watching the door.
cells.place: the opening where what's arriving comes in

cells.tense: You're making something happen and calling it the thing that's happening to you.
cells.ask: Name one outcome you set in motion this week and say 'mine' about it out loud once, no explanation attached.
cells.core: Something's coming together and you talk about it like luck. The thing that worked, the timing that landed, the door that opened — as if none of it came from a choice. Saying plainly what you did, without ceremony, and letting it count — that part is done well when the story has you in it, doing the verbs. There's a moment you picked the direction and kept picking it, and you skip past that part when you tell it.\n\nTry one sentence about something you made, with you in it. No bow, no policy statement. Just: this came from a hand, and it's here now. That's the piece you get to keep — the saying-so, not the thing.
cells.sheetLine: You've been making this and calling it luck.
cells.place: the opening where what's arriving comes in
